newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamist PM says no alternative to his rule.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamist PM says no alternative to his rule.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday that the opposition could not mount a credible alternative to his coalition government.
"Either arithmetically or actually, there is no alternative," Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, told parliamentary deputies from his Welfare Party.
Erbakan, faced with growing challenges to his rule from the army and others in the secularist establishment, said in the same speech he was prepared for new elections at any moment.

A row between the Islamists and the military over religious activism threatens to topple the 10-month-old coalition and opposition leaders have begun a search for a new "Islamist-free" government formula.
Leftist leader Bulent Ecevit was meeting other opposition leaders for talks on forming an alternative, "Islamist-free" government.

Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller has so far stood by Erbakan, but his Islam-based Welfare Party has made clear it is not prepared to go along with some military demands for a crackdown on a religious revival.
